name: Elephant
description: Deep memory intelligence with infrasonic communication, multi-generational spatial knowledge, and empathic social bonding across vast distances.

core_attributes.pattern: infrasonic communication, spatial memory mapping, social bonding

scope.definition: Maximum effective communication range of elephant infrasonic calls (14-35 Hz) under savanna conditions — distance at which call amplitude remains detectable above ambient noise, measured by playback array.

evidence.source: Payne et al. (1986) 'Infrasonic calls of the Asian elephant', Behavioral Ecology and Sociobiology 18:297-301; McComb et al. (2003) 'Long-distance communication of acoustic cues to social identity', Animal Behaviour.
cross_domain_examples: infrasonic calls detected by seismic sensors 10 km from source — ground propagation supplements airborne
elephant herds coordinate movement across 4 km separation using infrasound during dry season
blue whale 20 Hz calls: analogous infrasonic long-range communication in marine environment

scope.falsifiability: If elephant herd coordination across >5 km is maintained in populations with experimentally blocked infrasonic frequency range, infrasound is not the primary long-range coordination mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Range is wind-direction dependent — calls travel further downwind. Thermal inversions can extend range to 15+ km. Road noise and seismic activity from mining significantly disrupt infrasonic communication.

scope.definition: Accuracy of elephant memory for water source locations — proportion of navigations to known water sources not visited in >12 months that result in successful location of the source within 5% of direct path.

evidence.source: Poole (1994) 'Sex differences in the behavior and social organization of African elephants', Advances in the Study of Behavior; Foley et al. (2008) elephant spatial memory study, Biology Letters.
cross_domain_examples: elephant matriarchs navigate to water sources not visited in 9+ years in drought conditions (Foley 2008)
GPS tracking shows 0.89 efficiency vs straight-line path for known-location water navigation
Clark's nutcracker bird: spatial memory for 10,000+ seed cache locations over 6-month interval

scope.falsifiability: If GPS-tracked elephants searching for distant water sources during drought show random (non-directed) movement indistinguishable from chance navigation, episodic spatial memory is not the guiding mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Spatial memory accuracy is matriarch-age-dependent — oldest females (50+) show highest precision. Landscape changes (new fences, vegetation loss) can make stored maps inaccurate.

scope.definition: Proportion of observed cases where elephants respond to conspecific distress signals (vocalizations, posture) with affiliative behavior (trunk touching, body contact) directed at the distressed individual.

evidence.source: Bates et al. (2008) 'Do elephants show empathy?', Journal of Consciousness Studies 15:204-225; Plotnik et al. (2011) 'Elephants know when they need a helping trunk in a cooperative task', PNAS 108:5116-5121.
cross_domain_examples: elephants respond to distress vocalizations of family members with directed consolation behavior in 0.87 of observed cases
cooperative bucket-pulling task: elephants wait for partner before pulling — delay indicates other-awareness
bonobo consolation behavior after aggression: kiss, embrace directed at loser within 60 s in 0.82 of cases

scope.falsifiability: If controlled experiments show elephant consolation behavior is directed randomly (not specifically toward distressed individuals), affiliative response is not targeted empathy.
scope.measurement_limits: Field observation has confirmation bias — distressing events draw observer attention. Captive elephant empathy studies show higher rates (0.93) possibly due to closer social bonds. Wild data is sparser.
